votes.motion: Approve the work session minutes of June 13, 2023; August 8, 2023 and August 15, 2023 as well as the formal meeting minutes of June 6, 2023 and August 15, 2023.
votes.description: Approval of multiple prior work session and formal meeting minutes as presented.

votes.motion: Adopt Joint Ceremonial Resolution 25 of 2023, recognizing September as National Suicide Prevention and Action Month.
votes.description: A joint ceremonial resolution with Mayor Mendenhall recognizing September as National Suicide Prevention and Action Month.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and refer Item B-1 (Grant Application: Summer Food Service Program 2023 for YouthCity) to a future Consent Agenda for action.
votes.description: Closes the public hearing on a USDA-funded grant application for daily snacks for YouthCity 2023 summer program youth and refers it to a future consent agenda.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and defer action on the Form Based Urban Neighborhood Zoning Text Amendment (Fleet Block) to a future Council Meeting.
votes.description: Closes the public hearing on proposed FB-MU11 zoning text and map amendments for the Fleet Block property and defers Council action to a future meeting.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and refer the Ivory University House Public Benefits Analysis item to a future date for action.
votes.description: Closes the public hearing on a resolution to adopt public benefit analysis conclusions and authorize fee waivers and refunds for Ivory University House L3C, referring it to a future meeting for action.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and refer the Budget Amendment No. 1 for Fiscal Year 2023-24 item to a future date for action.
votes.description: Closes the public hearing on the FY2023-24 Budget Amendment No. 1 ordinance and defers Council action to a future meeting.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and adopt Ordinance 49 of 2023, amending the Consolidated Fee Schedule for Fiscal Year 2024 related to land and sidewalk closure fees.
votes.description: Closes the public hearing and adopts an ordinance amending the Salt Lake City Consolidated Fee Schedule to separately address lane and sidewalk closure fees.

votes.motion: Reject the ordinance for the 1782 South 1600 East Zoning Map and Master Plan Amendment.
votes.description: Rejects the proposed ordinance that would have rezoned 1782 South 1600 East from R-1/7000 to SR-3 and amended the Sugar House Future Land Use Map.

votes.motion: Pass a legislative action requesting staff study a zoning text amendment to consider amending all R-1 single-family zones, including consolidating R-1/5,000, 7,000, and 12,000 into one zone, reducing minimum lot size, removing or reducing minimum frontage, easing flag lot standards, and allowing single-family attached housing in all zones; and initiate a separate study to consider zoning map amendments along collector and arterial roads to allow greater residential density and mixed-use developments.
votes.description: Directs staff to conduct a comprehensive study of R-1 zoning text amendments and a separate study of zoning map amendments along collector and arterial roads for increased density and mixed-use development.

votes.motion: That the City collaborate with the County to get a better understanding of how City and County ordinances interact pertaining to the lot subdivision process and update ordinances if needed to make sure both are consistent (second paragraph removed via friendly amendment by Councilmember Wharton, accepted by Councilmember Valdemoros).
votes.description: Directs the City to collaborate with Salt Lake County to review and align City and County ordinances related to the lot subdivision process.

votes.motion: Include in the legislative action that the Council will hold a work session with the Administration on the scope of the study to include: alignment with Thriving in Place, alignment with future land/water policy, alignment with public transportation needs, and the vision of a walkable city (amended via friendly amendment by Councilmember Mano to incorporate the four points into the first study, accepted by Councilmember Dugan).
votes.description: Adds four policy alignment considerations to the scope of the R-1 zoning text amendment study to be addressed in a work session with the Administration.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 53 of 2023, prohibiting all new drive-through facilities in the Sugar House Business Districts CSHBD1 and CSHBD2.
votes.description: Adopts an ordinance amending Title 21A to remove drive-through facilities as a permitted or conditional use in the Sugar House Business District zones CSHBD1 and CSHBD2.

Approves all items on the consent agenda, including a grant for Jordan River debris removal, setting a public hearing date for the Rose Park Lane annexation and zoning amendment, and four board appointments to the Library Board and Planning Commission.
